title: Upwork Monthly Hiring Insights: AI is changing the marketing skills businesses hire for
summary: Upwork’s October's hiring report points to changing needs within marketing.
body_markdown:
## AI is changing the marketing skills businesses hire for


October’s hiring data points to changing needs within marketing. AI advertising and SEO skills recorded consecutive months of contract growth, while demand for “Banner Ad Design” and “SEO Backlinking” declined both year over year and month over month.


These patterns echo our[recent research with OpenAI’s Economic Research team](https://www.upwork.com/research/ai-how-work-comes-together) , which found AI-related projects combining established and AI-related tasks in new ways. Together, the findings suggest how work can change within familiar roles before job titles change.


Beyond marketing, software quality stood out: testing skills accounted for three of the five leading positions among skills growing both year over year and month over month.


“A marketing role may keep its title while the work changes,” said Jennifer Brett, managing director of the Upwork Research Institute. “October’s hiring patterns point to opportunities for professionals who combine marketing expertise with AI skills, from shaping generated video into effective advertising to helping businesses navigate changes in search. Understanding audiences and campaign goals remains essential as the tools and tasks evolve.”


## Top hiring insights for October 2026


- **AI advertising is creating opportunities to apply creative expertise in new ways** . “AI Ad Creation” recorded three consecutive months of contract growth, and “AI Video Ads” grew for two, while “Banner Ad Design” declined both monthly and annually. The opportunity for creative professionals is to combine AI fluency with the judgment needed to deliver effective advertising.
- **Search marketing’s changing skill needs are showing up in hiring** . “AI SEO” recorded a second consecutive month of contract growth, while “SEO Backlinking” declined both monthly and annually. The contrast may reflect businesses adapting to AI’s role in search, creating opportunities for specialists who can help them navigate how customers find information.
- **Software quality is a standout hiring priority** . “Software Testing,” “Functional Testing,” and “Usability Testing” occupied three of the five leading positions among skills growing both year over year and month over month. Businesses are hiring for expertise that helps turn software into reliable, usable products.


## Testing expertise helps turn software into reliable products


The skills demand data below capture what Upwork Marketplace clients hired for in October compared with October 2025 and September 2026. The quadrant chart shows how skills demand changed across both periods.


“Software Testing,” “Functional Testing,” and “Usability Testing” ranked second, third, and fourth in the growing-and-accelerating quadrant. Together, they cover several dimensions of product quality: identifying software issues, checking that features work as intended, and assessing how easily people can use a product.


‍[September’s](https://www.upwork.com/research/upwork-monthly-hiring-insights-september-2026) report highlighted searches for specialists who build AI products and systems. October adds a parallel hiring signal: demand for the expertise needed to test functionality and usability. The data do not link the testing contracts directly to AI projects, but they show that product quality is an active area of hiring.


“Unreal Engine,” a platform used to develop games and other interactive 3D experiences, ranked first in the quadrant. "Claude" ranked fifth, returning to monthly growth after a decline in[August](https://www.upwork.com/research/upwork-monthly-hiring-insights-august-2026) .


###### Figure 1: Skills demand momentum quadrant, October 2026


*Source: Upwork Marketplace data, October 2026 compared with October 2025 and September 2026*


Other skills showed mixed momentum. “Data Annotation,” “Data Labeling,” and “Video Editing Software” remained above year-earlier levels but declined from September. “Android” and “iOS” grew month over month while remaining below October 2025 levels. Demand for some traditional marketing activities, “Banner Ad Design” and “SEO Backlinking” declined both year over year and month over month.


## AI advertising hiring shows sustained growth


“AI Ad Creation” and “AI Animation Tools” each recorded three consecutive months of contract growth. “AI Video Ads” grew for two months.


**This sustained demand suggests that AI is changing the skills businesses seek in advertising** , creating opportunities for marketing professionals who combine AI fluency with creative judgment and an understanding of audiences and campaign goals. The trend points to how marketing roles can evolve as AI becomes part of the production process, with human expertise remaining essential to turning generated content into effective advertising.


### AI SEO grows as backlinking demand declines


As people turn to LLMs and Google’s AI Overviews for answers, businesses face a new challenge: making their brands visible in AI-generated responses. On the Upwork Marketplace, “AI SEO” recorded a second consecutive month of contract growth, while demand for a more traditional activity within search engine optimization, “SEO Backlinking,” declined.


**The divergence may reflect changing priorities in search marketing** , as businesses seek expertise to navigate AI’s growing role in how customers find them.

## The AI Signal


### AI video searches point to specific advertising needs


“AI video” remained the most-searched AI-related term for a[second consecutive month](https://www.upwork.com/research/upwork-monthly-hiring-insights-september-2026) . “AI video creator,” “AI video generator,” and “AI video editor” also appeared among the ten most-searched terms, showing continued client interest across the production process.


Technical expertise remained prominent: “AI developer” ranked second, while “AI automation,” “AI engineer,” and “AI agent” also appeared in the top ten.


###### Figure 3: Top 10 AI-related search terms on the Upwork Marketplace, October 2026


*Source: Upwork Marketplace data, October 2026*


“AI UGC video” (AI-generated video in the style of creator or user-generated content) was October’s fastest-growing AI-related search year over year. “AI video ads” ranked fourth, while “AI video editor” and “AI video creator” also made the top ten.


Together, these searches show clients specifying both the content they want and the expertise needed to produce it. **The sustained growth points to opportunities for marketing professionals who combine AI fluency with creative judgment.** As AI becomes part of advertising production, expertise in shaping content for an audience and campaign remains valuable.


This builds on[recent months](https://www.upwork.com/research/upwork-monthly-hiring-insights-august-2026) ’ interest in AI creative production, with advertising offering a concrete example of how businesses want to apply the technology.


Technical implementation also continues to feature in client searches. “AI agent developer” and “AI SaaS developer” ranked second and third among the fastest-growing AI-related queries, extending September’s interest in specialists who can build AI into products and systems.

## About the Upwork Monthly Hiring Insights Report


The Upwork Monthly Hiring Insights Report provides an early signal of broader shifts in how business leaders are hiring. It offers a complementary, more granular picture of trends in the U.S. labor market, with a focus on the independent talent economy.


### Methodology


**Skill demand quadrant methodology** Skills demand is measured by the number of distinct hired contracts whose job post mentions the skill in a given month, across U.S. marketplace clients. Each skill must meet minimum volume thresholds — at least 100 contracts in the current month and 50 in the comparison period. Year-over-year (YoY) change compares the current month's contract count to the same month one year prior. Month-over-month (MoM) change compares to the immediately preceding month. Skills are assigned to one of four quadrants based on the sign of each metric:


*Growing & Accelerating*


YoY Growth & MoM Growth — demand is higher than last year and still accelerating


*Growing & Cooling*


YoY Growth & MoM Decline — demand is higher than last year but cooling from a recent peak


*Declining & Recovering*


YoY Decline & MoM Growth — demand is lower than last year but showing short-term recovery


*Declining*


YoY Decline & MoM Decline — demand is lower than last year and continuing to decline


Within each quadrant, the top 5 skills are ranked by a composite score suited to the quadrant's character: for the top left and bottom right quadrants, skills are ranked by the sum of their YoY and MoM change to surface those with the strongest combined signal; for the top right, by YoY change alone (since MoM is negative by definition); and for the bottom left, by MoM change alone (since YoY is negative by definition).


**Demand persistence methodology** Demand persistence measures how many consecutive months a skill's hired contract count has increased, inclusive of the current month. A skill qualifies if it has at least 20 contracts in the current month and has gained at least 10 contracts in absolute terms over the duration of its streak. These lower thresholds (compared to the quadrant analysis) are intentional — persistent growth is most editorially interesting for emerging skills that have not yet reached mainstream volume. For the AI-specific persistence view, skills are further filtered to those matching a curated list of AI-related keywords.


**Search data** AI-related search terms were identified by matching raw client search queries against a curated AI-related keyword list. The volume ranking reflects total search occurrences within the month. The growth ranking measures year-over-year changes and compares current-month search counts against the same month one year prior, filtered to queries with at least 50 current-month and 20 prior-year occurrences to exclude low-volume noise.
